messages:
Kyle: Heads-up — canary cluster r-az3 saw a p99 latency jump ~2.4x at 03:12UTC after the driver roll. Appears correlated with kernel autoselect flipflopping between Triton matmul and FlashAttention path.
Maria: saw that on dashboards, thanks. Any noisy-tenant indications on that host?
Kyle: noisy-tenant low signal. The thing that stands out is KV cache eviction rate spiking. When autoselect switches to flash path, memory workspace changes and we see more KV evictions -> smaller batches -> p99 up.
Devon: dump of the selector trace from the node: 
```
[selector] input_len=64 batch_est=24 -> chose=triton_gemm_preferred
[selector] input_len=64 batch_est=8  -> chose=flash_attn_fallback
[selector] input_len=16 batch_est=4  -> chose=flash_attn
[selector] runtime_mem=22.1GB free=1.2GB -> switch heuristic triggered
```
Ashley: that runtime_mem/free line looks suspicious — driver 530.x has a different workspace accounting. Did the deploy change kernel workspace assumptions?
Kyle: Exactly. After the CUDA/driver patch, kernel workspace reported free memory lower, so the heuristic thinks it must pick lower-memory kernels (flash path) even though throughput would be better with GEMM for these seq-length distributions.
Maria: Can you attach a short perf profile for one of the problematic requests? even just top kernel durations.
Kyle: pasted from perf log (short):
```
req id: r-23aa
seqs: [8, 16, 64, 64, 8]
profile:
  triton_gemm: 1.8ms (40%)
  flash_attn: 2.9ms (65%)
  kv_lookup: 0.9ms (20%)
  dispatch_overhead: 0.6ms
```
note: when autoselect flips, triton_gemm disappears and flash_attn goes to 4.5ms due to smaller effective batch.

Devon: TLDR: driver workspace reporting change -> selector picks flash kernels more often -> KV cache eviction increases -> batching heuristic produces smaller batches -> p99 spike.
Ashley: any quick mitigation we can push? a) pin selector to prefer GEMM on the node, b) increase KV cache budget, or c) roll driver back.
Maria: I can patch the selector config to bias toward GEMM for the canary pool (low-risk). Will that be safe?
Kyle: yes please, set selector.bias_override = {prefer: "triton_gemm", ttl: 30m} for r-az3 nodes. That should reduce oscillation while we investigate.
Maria: doing it now. config change: 
```
POST /admin/selector/override
{
  "pool": "r-az3-canary",
  "prefer": "triton_gemm",
  "ttl": "30m",
  "author": "maria"
}
```

infra-bot: config applied to 3 nodes in r-az3-canary by Maria.
Kyle: after override I see p99 trending down already in Grafana. Good.
Devon: For root cause, we need to reproduce locally: run kernel probe with driver version X+1 and compare workspace query values. I can spin up a test VM.
Ashley: I'll capture a KV eviction trace and batching heatmap for the next hour. If the driver's workspace API changed semantics, we should file a bug with vendor and treat as reg-critical.
Maria: Also let's add a quick heuristic patch: treat reported free memory < configured_workspace_margin as suspect if driver_version >= "530.8" and require two consecutive samples before switching kernels. Small debounce should stop flipflop.
Kyle: agree. That debounce will avoid thrash. Devon — can you PR that? keep it small and feature-flagged.
Devon: on it. Will target a hotfix branch and request review. PR will include unit tests and a canary flag.
Kyle: SRE-Bot has created incident I-2026-034 for tracking.
SRE-Bot: Incident I-2026-034 created. Summary: canary p99 spike due to kernel autoselect oscillation after driver update.
Ashley: quick note — if we later roll forward with new driver, we should validate workspace accounting in our integration tests to catch this earlier. Adding test ticket to backlog.
Maria: rollback not needed if override + debounce hold. I'll monitor for 2 hours then remove override.
Kyle: thanks all. Follow-ups: Devon PR, Ashley heatmap upload, Maria monitor + remove override after stable. :thumbsup:
Maria: uploading KV eviction trace and heatmap to the incident thread now -> https://internal.redwood/incident/I-2026-034/artifacts
Kyle: leaving logs + selector traces in the incident. If vendor patch comes back, we will validate and remove debounce.
Maria: closing loop: p99 back to normal on canary for 45m. Keeping incident open for further validation on dedicated pools.
